stanza: Ophelia, she's 'neath the window
For her I feel so afraid
On her twenty-second birthday
She already is an old maid
To her, death is quite romantic
She wears an iron vest
Her profession's her religion
Her sin is her lifelessness
And though her eyes are fixed upon
Noah's great rainbow
She spends her time peeking
Into Desolation Row

peaking.line: Twenty-eight years have passed, I feel I'm peaking
peaking.linePrev: Black not white, red all over though, like Elmo

speaking.songTitle: The King of Carrot Flowers, Pt. One
speaking.line: And your mom would drink until she was no longer speaking
stanza: And this is the room one afternoon, I knew I could love you
And from above you how I sank into your soul
Into that secret place where no one dares to go
And your mom would drink until she was no longer speaking
And dad would dream of all the different ways to die
Each one a little more than he could dare to try
And in the naked light I saw
Ten thousand people, maybe more
People talking without speaking
People hearing without listening
People writing songs that voices never share
And no one dared
Disturb the sound of silence
I'd follow you forever
Even without looking
You call, we come together
Even without speaking

speaking.line: Show me the ways I forgot to be speaking
speaking.linePrev: Show me the things I've been missing
speaking.lineNext: Show me the ways to get back to the garden

stanza: Speakers speaking
Speakers speaking
Speaking in code

speaking.line: I wanted to believe in all the words that I was speaking
stanza: I wanted to believe in all the words that I was speaking
As we moved together in the dark
And all the friends that I was telling, all the playful misspellings
And every bite I gave that left a mark
When tiny vessels oozed into your neck and formed the bruises
That you said you didn't want to fade
But they did, and so did I that day

speaking.line: Unable to listen, we keep speaking
speaking.linePrev: I'm okay with that, too proud
speaking.lineNext: Moted by blood, unable to notice ourselves

stanza: You won't be happy with me
But give me one more chance
You won't be happy anyway
Why do we still live here
In this repulsive town?
All our friends are in New York
Why do we keep shrieking
When we mean soft things?
We should be whispering all the time
